name: blast-visual-full
description: Comprehensive visual pipeline test covering all 7 blast system areas: drill plan, charge/sequence, software preview tiers, detonation execution, post-blast report, and voxel fragmentation with multi-angle screenshots at every stage

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from $50,000 to $150,000 -- drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action, so this file needs a driller/drill_rig it never used to, on top of the four blast-workshop software tiers it already buys. Bumped again to $200,000 (#554): charging is now real work too -- three separate charge orders (Charge All plus two per-hole overrides), each drained by its own wait, add several hundred more ticks of the 3-driller roster's payroll/fuel upkeep before the tier:4 software purchase further down this file (observed short by ~10,400 at $150,000).

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed any roster before its drill_plan) now needs one first. Employee #1.

#553 crew-walkout fix (issue #586 CI): a single driller working a 3x4=12-hole pattern unattended for the hundreds of real ticks drilling now takes runs well-being to 0 (no Living Quarters anywhere in this file) long before the pattern finishes -- WORKER REVOLT fires and its full-screen game-over overlay blocks every subsequent panel click, which is exactly the `clickSelector "#bs-blast-panel [data-step=\"2\"]" failed: element is covered by div` CI failure. Command-mode traces (sandbox-measured) confirmed a single driller only lands 9 of 12 holes before the revolt fires at tick ~235, and even a second driller alone still revolts right as hole #12 lands (razor-thin, confirmed on this exact seed). A `living_quarters` was tried too and made things strictly worse: it doesn't slow the well-being crash meaningfully at this crew size, and it introduces a genuine rest/re-collapse thrash that permanently stalls drilling a few holes in (reproduced with 1 and 2 drillers, holeCount frozen through 2000+ ticks) -- not something this scenario file can route around, so it's left out. What works: a second driller/drill_rig pair for parallel drilling (this employee, #2) plus one more, unrigged, purely idle driller (employee #3 below) whose fresh, untouched needs pull the average morale that feeds the well-being score up for as long as it stays idle -- both employees are cheap ($1000 each) next to a third drill_rig ($35,000), and the combination keeps well-being comfortably above 0 until the pattern is nearly done instead of pinned at 0 for hundreds of ticks.

#553 crew-walkout fix: employee #3, deliberately left unrigged and unskilled -- it never drives, never drills, never leaves the office. Its only job is to sit on a full needs bar so the roster's average morale (and therefore the well-being score, ScoreManager.ts) doesn't collapse to 0 as fast as it would with only the two working drillers on site. Sandbox-measured: with this employee in the roster, well-being is still 69.6 at tick 50 and doesn't hit 0 until tick ~250-300, instead of tick ~150 with just two working drillers -- enough margin that the 120-tick WORKER REVOLT countdown (REVOLT_TICKS, balance.ts) never matures before the pattern finishes drilling.
#553: vehicle #1.

#553 crew-walkout fix: vehicle #2, for the second driller (employee #2) -- see the employee-hire steps above for why. Two drillers working the pattern concurrently roughly halves the ticks needed to land all 12 holes versus one alone (sandbox-measured: 12/12 by tick ~285-300 instead of stalling at 9/12 past the revolt point).

Grants the driller (employee #1) the licence to drive the drill_rig just purchased -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow); left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is blast execution, not re-proving vehicle licensing.
Same bootstrap licence grant as employee #1, above, for the second driller. Employee #3 (the idle relief hire) deliberately gets no skill and no vehicle -- see its own hire step.

#553 crew-walkout fix: crews drill_rig #1 with driller #1 explicitly. Sandbox-measured: with two rigs and three employees (only two of them qualified), the auto-board dispatch that a single lone driller/rig pair could rely on picks an inconsistent pairing and one hole is permanently left undrilled -- explicit `vehicle driver` assignment (same convention as level3-playthrough-win.json's own two-driller crewing) removes the ambiguity. Does NOT re-click the vehicles toolbar tab: the panel is already open, left that way by the preceding `vehicle buy drill_rig` (vehicle #2) step -- the two `employee assign_skill` bootstrap steps in between use `command` type, not a click, so panel state is unchanged. UIManager.togglePanel closes an ALREADY-active panel on re-click instead of leaving it open (same class of bug already fixed elsewhere in this PR), which is what made this step's own assign button resolve to zero size.
Crews drill_rig #2 with driller #2, same reasoning as the step above.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:4 spacing:5 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Two increment clicks on the spacing stepper (data-field="spacing") raise it 3->5m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) before dragging, so the (20,20)-(35,30) rectangle computes the declared 4x3 instead of the default-spacing 6x4 (issue #479 follow-up, Finding #4). depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: drill_plan now only orders holes -- holeCount stays 0 until the driller actually drives the drill_rig to each one and drills it, proven by the wait step below.

#553: waits for the two drillers to drive their drill_rigs to all 12 ordered holes and drill them (sandbox-measured: lands around tick 285-300 with two concurrent driller/drill_rig pairs). Six rounds of tick 50 (with a defensive event-resolve after each) cover that -- deliberately not more: with a lone driller this used to run seven rounds (350 ticks), but every extra round past the sixth pushes well-being's already-flat 0 streak (no Living Quarters in this file, see the employee-hire steps above) past the 120-tick WORKER REVOLT threshold (REVOLT_TICKS, balance.ts) with all 12 holes already drilled and nothing left to wait for -- sandbox-confirmed: a seventh round here does trigger the revolt's blocking game-over overlay.
Long enough for the two drillers to land the last of the 12 ordered holes.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Per-hole charging is a real control now (gap G3, ChargeHoleList.ts): the Charge step renders a "Per Hole" section, one row per hole keyed by data-hole, each with its own commit button at [data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="charge-hole"]. That button dispatches `charge hole:<id> explosive:<selected> amount:<amount>kg stemming:<stemming>m` from the panel's current product card / amount / stemming values (ChargeStep.chargeHole, Charge.ts) — the same three values Charge All reads, so the steppers have to be driven to the declared numbers first. The Charge All step above already pinned the panel to [data-step="2"] (a manual tab click disarms autoAdvance), so the Per Hole rows stay visible. 3 amount increments (5 -> 8kg) and 5 stemming increments (2.0 -> 3.0m) reach this hole's declared values. Amount steps by 1kg (data-field="amount", clamped to the selected product's [minChargeKg, maxChargeKg]); stemming steps by 0.2m with a 0.5m floor (data-field="stemming", Charge.ts adjustStemming). Both are plain instance fields on ChargeStep with no reset path, so they carry over from the previous charge step in the same page session — asserted before each commit rather than assumed.

expect.note: count is unchanged — every hole was already charged by Charge All; this step overrides H1 alone

steps.description: #554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.
The opposite override on the neighbouring hole: 5 amount decrements (8 -> 3kg) and 10 stemming decrements (3.0 -> 1.0m) off what the H1 row left behind, then H2's own commit button.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Per-hole delay is a relative +/- stepper ([data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="delay-inc"/"delay-dec"], Sequence.ts), stepping by the panel's current delay-step value and clamping at 0. Reaching an exact target is therefore arithmetic on the delay Auto Sequence actually assigned, read out of a real command-mode trace (screenshots/scenario-<name>-command/step-NN-sequence.json's sequenceDelays) rather than computed by re-deriving autoVPattern. Auto Sequence left H1 at 50ms with a 25ms step (traced: step-08-sequence.json), so 2 decrements land exactly on the declared 0 (50 -> 25 -> 0); a third would be a no-op, since adjustHoleDelay floors the result at 0.

expect.note: H1 50ms -> 25 -> 0; no hole gains or loses a delay, only H1's value changes

steps.description: Auto Sequence already put H6 on exactly this step's declared 100ms (traced: step-08-sequence.json), so the arithmetic here is a net zero — one increment and one decrement (100 -> 125 -> 100) is the honest click expression of it, and it still exercises both stepper directions on a row other than H1. Command mode's version of this step was likewise a no-op: the step-08 and step-09 dumps are byte-identical.

expect.note: H6 ends on 100ms, the same value it started this step with
